question: Is the champion measurably worse on a covariate-defined slice (sparse rating-key rows), and does a smoother family repair that slice when gated in?

why_new.measured_motivation: reports/phase19/shared_error_atlas.json: rows whose (13 ratings + Class + Type of Travel + Customer Type) key occurs exactly once (254,260 rows, 36.3%) have port AUC 0.950323 versus 0.961853 pooled. Sparse-key rows cannot use any key-level lookup and must be ranked by a smooth function of the remaining covariates.
prior_attempts: ENS72 covariate gating over hundreds of covariates: +1.01e-5 over the equal blend, could not generalise
feat48/feat51 hierarchical rating blocks: absorbed on the rich view
why_new.material_difference: The gate variable is label-free (a train-set frequency of a feature key), the gate has exactly one fitted parameter per segment, and the composition outside the segment is left at the champion. Selection risk is therefore O(1 parameter x 5 folds), not O(285 covariates).

segments.S1_unique_key: train frequency of the 16-column rating key == 1
segments.S2_sparse_key: train frequency of the 16-column rating key <= 3

frozen_family.vectors: for each of 8 name-defined families (lgbm, xgb, cat, realmlp, tabm, tabpfn, blend, histgb) take the stored OOF vector with the best standalone pooled AUC whose name starts with a declared prefix for that family; the rule is deterministic and does not depend on the segment result
frozen_family.fitting: per fold, the gate weight is chosen to maximise AUC on the FIT rows that fall inside the segment; it is applied only to eval-fold rows inside the segment; rows outside the segment keep the champion logit exactly

statistics: mean paired per-fold delta vs the champion and its paired fold SE over 5 folds
Holm adjustment over the 16 frozen tests
failure_conditions: gate weight fitted on eval-fold rows (leakage; the implementation asserts FIT/eval disjointness by construction)
champion vector hash mismatch against the certified OOF
any segment definition using the target

leakage_analysis.segment_definition: label-free: hash frequency over the 16 feature columns of the TRAIN rows only, computed without the target
leakage_analysis.multiple_testing_disclosure: Holm covers the 16 frozen tests only; it does not cover the ~600 historical experiments or prior use of the primary folds.

expected_outcome: Given the 7% parent-improvement conversion ratio measured on the internal2->internal4 route audit (route +5.34e-5 -> portfolio +3.818e-6), a segment-local repair of a 36%-row slice would need a very large slice-local gain to reach the gate. A null result is the expected and still informative outcome.
